figures.finding: Serbia and Montenegro no longer exists as a state: Montenegro voted for independence on 21 May 2006 and applied to join the UN as its own member, so no agreement, fund or incentive of Serbia and Montenegro applies today; film work on its former territory follows Serbia's rules (RS) or Montenegro's (ME).
figures.applies: Former state union of Serbia and Montenegro, from June 2006.

sources.said: the Security Council today considered an application by the Republic of Montenegro, which recently voted for independence from Serbia, to join the world body.

Montenegro’s request for admission came in a letter to Secretary-General Kofi Annan from its President, Filip Vujanovic, and followed an independence referendum held in the country on 21 May. If admitted, Montenegro would become the UN’s 192nd Member State.

Serbia Note 1. As from 3 June 2006: “Serbia”. Formerly: “Serbia and Montenegro” until 2 June 2006. The Republic of Serbia continued the membership of Serbia and Montenegro in the United Nations, including all organs and organizations of the United Nations system, … Montenegro was admitted to membership in the United Nations by General Assembly resolution A/RES/60/264 on 28 June 2006.

figures.finding: Serbia and Montenegro was called Serbia from 3 June 2006: the Republic of Serbia continued its UN membership, and Montenegro was admitted to the UN as a new member on 28 June 2006.
